advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether an explicit `--caused-by` naming an already-linked culprit should upgrade a stale 'derived' provenance to 'explicit' (currently the `culprit in existing` early return leaves it 'derived').
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:239: `if not culprit or culprit == ticket_id or culprit in existing:`
provenance write only reached after the guard: `provenance = "explicit" if caused_by.strip() else "derived"` at line 250-251
docstring at lines 224-228 documents replacing a DIFFERENT explicit culprit but not upgrading provenance on the same already-linked culprit
advisory.finding: An explicit `--caused-by` that names an ALREADY-linked culprit does not upgrade that edge's provenance from 'derived' to 'explicit': `_apply_caused_by` returns early at the `culprit in existing` guard before reaching the provenance-bearing `_write_link_event`, so an edge auto-derived on a prior close stays labeled 'derived' even after the operator explicitly confirms the same culprit — the provenance metric counts a now-proven attribution as a guess.
scenarios: A bug is closed with blame auto-derivation (edge written 'derived'); the operator reopens and re-closes with an explicit `--caused-by <same-culprit>` to confirm the attribution — the edge remains 'derived'.
Metrics `bug_caused_by_provenance` reports the confirmed edge under 'derived' rather than 'explicit'.

evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:239: `if not culprit or culprit == ticket_id or culprit in existing:` then `return`
`_active_caused_by_targets` returns target ids regardless of provenance (transition_close.py:175-181), so a prior `derived` edge to the same culprit lands in `existing`
The provenance write (`provenance = "explicit" if caused_by.strip() else "derived"`, line 250) is only reached after the guard, so the same-target explicit correction never rewrites the edge
advisory.finding: In `_apply_caused_by`, the `culprit in existing` early-return guard fires before any provenance write, so re-closing a bug (after reopen) with an explicit `--caused-by` naming the SAME target already recorded as a blame-`derived` edge does NOT upgrade the stored provenance to `explicit`; the operator's explicit attribution of an already-linked culprit is silently ignored.

Ticket 6536-367c Scope enumerates: _links.py, transition_close.py, _processors.py, common.schema.json, bug_trends.py, docs/event-schema.md, docs/user-guide.md, and the two test files — scripts/backfill_caused_by.py is NOT among them (it is only a plan-review read-path).

advisory.suggested_fix: If the backfill-marking behavior is desired, add scripts/backfill_caused_by.py to the ticket's file_impact/Scope (it is a legitimate producer of derived edges, per the event-schema doc) so the change is explicitly authorized rather than a drive-by.

evidence: tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py:118-123 asserts only target_id: `return [d["target_id"] for d in deps ...]` then `assert _caused_by(sc_bug) == [culprit]` — no provenance assertion
tests/unit/test_caused_by_provenance.py docstring lists close and link paths but NOT the backfill script; search of tests for `backfill` + `provenance` shows no overlap
dropped.finding: The backfill script's newly-added `provenance="derived"` marking is not asserted by any test. scripts/backfill_caused_by.py now writes `_write_link_event(bug_id, culprit_id, "caused_by", tracker_dir, provenance="derived")`, but the existing e2e test (tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py::test_end_to_end_exactly_one_link_from_two_bugs) asserts only `_caused_by(sc_bug) == [culprit]` (target ids) and `n == 1` — never the provenance value. A regression dropping or mislabeling the backfill provenance (e.g. reverting to no marker, so backfilled guesses read as 'unknown', or setting 'explicit', so guesses read as proven) would pass every test.
